name: metric-mover-offline
description: Explains why a metric moved from a before/after table you paste into the chat, broken down by segment (channel, country, platform, plan...). Code computes everything: each segment's contribution, mix shift versus rate change for conversion-style rates (with counts), how concentrated the change is, new or vanished segments, a Simpson's-paradox check and two-proportion significance tests. It returns up to six ranked hypotheses, each backed by computed evidence and a generic way to confirm it, and a measurement-artifact hypothesis whenever data quality could explain the move. It never states a cause as fact and never forecasts. Follow-ups work on the same table: by <dimension> only, top 3, show the numbers, as json, add event: <date> <what happened>, ignore <segment>. Up to 5,000 rows and 4 segment columns. It reads only what you give it: no warehouse, files or web, and no general questions.

skills.name: Explain a metric move
skills.description: Ranked, evidence-backed hypotheses for why a metric changed, from a pasted before/after table by segment, with the decomposition computed in code, plus follow-ups on the same table.
examples: Signups dropped; here is before/after by channel and country: <paste the table>
Revenue by plan, last week vs this week: <paste the table>
Add event: Oct 14 deploy of the new checkout
